T=1 represented ~6% of EncA particles purified from M. xanthus. Among recombinant empty EncA shells expressed in E. coli, T=1 represented ~20% in McHugh et al. 2014 and ~36% in Eren et al. 2022. Recombinant T=1 shells were observed only in the absence of co-expressed cargo in Eren et al. 2022. No inner diameter or wall thickness was directly reported for the T=1 shell. Assuming a spherical cavity, a spherical-equivalent inner diameter of ~11.9 nm can be estimated from the reported inner volume (8.71 × 10^5 Å³), corresponding to an approximate wall thickness of ~3.1 nm using the ~18 nm outer diameter. Yadav & Beck 2026 demonstrated that WT EncA T=1 formation during reassembly is strongly promoted by phosphate buffer and by conditions that disfavor the competing T=3 pathway. Once formed, T=1 shells are kinetically trapped and do not interconvert with T=3 upon buffer exchange.
